b1-unit-49.49.1 Gap Year Diaries: the secret of a l:
Danny: Welcome back to Gap Year Diaries! Today I'm not at the hostel. I'm in a small apartment in São Paulo with a very special guest. Ana's grandmother Lourdes turned ninety-seven last week, and she agreed to share her secrets with us. Ana is here too.
Ana: Hi everyone!
Lourdes: Good afternoon, young man. Ask me anything. But speak slowly!
Danny: So what's the secret of a long life?
Lourdes: Oh, there's no secret. I just never stopped moving. I grew up on a farm, and we worked from sunrise to sunset. Now I walk to the bakery every morning. It's only two blocks, but I walk.
Ana: And she still takes the stairs when the elevator is broken!
Danny: What about food?
Lourdes: Rice and beans, vegetables from the street market and fruit every day. Meat only on Sundays. And a little piece of dark chocolate after lunch. Just one!
Danny: Did you ever smoke?
Lourdes: Never. My husband smoked for twenty years. He quit when he was forty, and he lived until eighty-eight. If he hadn't quit, he wouldn't have lived so long. I'm sure of that.
Danny: Do you have any regrets?
Lourdes: Just one. I left school at twelve to help on the farm. If I had stayed in school, I would have become a teacher. I loved books.
Ana: But Grandma, you taught all of us to read!
Lourdes: That's true. And if I hadn't gone to that church party, I wouldn't have met your grandfather. So life worked out in the end.
Danny: What else keeps you young?
Lourdes: People! I play cards with my neighbors every Thursday, and one of my grandchildren calls me every night. And I don't worry about things I can't change. Worrying doesn't add a single day to your life.
Danny: Ana, you're a doctor. What do you think?
Ana: Good genes may be part of the reason. But I think the main reason is her lifestyle. She's always active, she eats well and she's never alone.
Danny: Any advice for our listeners?
Lourdes: Eat your vegetables, call your grandmother... and stop looking at your phone all day!
